channel.title: Megajournal Feed
channel.description: Aggregated research articles from the multidisciplinary megajournals: Nature Communications, restricted to biological and health sciences, and Science Advances, which is not filtered by subject because no accessible source exposes one.

item.title: Nature Communications: An LRR-truncated NLR natural variant confers dual resistance to drought and blast in rice
item.description: Genetic resources with combined resistance to drought and blast disease are scarce. Here, the authors identify NLR8 - Hap2, a natural allele of the rice NLR gene NLR8 that encodes an LRR-truncated protein, and show that it enhances resistance to both stresses by stabilizing two distinct transcription factors.

item.title: Nature Communications: XPO1-mediated TRIM21 nuclear export reprograms TREM2+ macrophage polarization by targeting IRF3 to augment anti-PD-1 efficacy in small cell lung cancer
item.description: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is an aggressive malignancy characterized by an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment (TME) resistant to Immune checkpoint inhibitor (ICI) therapy. Here, the authors define an XPO1-TRIM21-TNFSF15 axis that promotes the polarization of immunosuppressive TREM2+ macrophages, which ultimately orchestrates immune exclusion by impairing antigen presentation. Importantly, targeting XPO1 enhances the efficacy of anti-PD1 immunotherapy in mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: A CRISPR-based ‘dam-break drainage’ sensing architecture for rapid, affordable and ultrasensitive pathogen detection
item.description: Nucleic acid testing is central to infectious-disease diagnosis, and methods which combine high sensitivity with operational simplicity and ease of interpretation are particularly desirable. Here the authors present their CRISPR-based ‘dam-break drainage’ chip, where a positive result is clearly visualised via the release of test liquid from a sample reservoir.

item.title: Nature Communications: Differential lipid selectivity of StARD phospholipid transporters revealed by native MS
item.description: Lipid transfer proteins organize intracellular lipid distribution. Here, the authors show that seemingly redundant phospholipid transfer proteins have distinct acyl chain preferences, and suggest that their tissue-specific expression levels and phosphorylation fine-tune membrane composition.

item.title: Nature Communications: HOMEODOMAIN-LIKE shapes chromatin architecture and rewires leaf epidermal patterns
item.description: How chromatin organization influences developmental decisions remains poorly understood. Here the authors report a chromatin organizer that maintains higher-order genome organization and coordinated gene expression to balance cell division and differentiation in plants.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structural basis of the gating mechanism of the large-conductance mechanosensitive channel from Escherichia coli
item.description: Here, authors solve three cryo-EM structures of EcMscL in two different lipid environments and two distinct conformational states; closed and open-like, guided by EPR. Additional EPR, MD and HDX-MS experiments provide insight into the gating mechanism.

item.title: Nature Communications: A somatic checkpoint through NHR-49/HNF4α governs reproductive investment and longevity in C. elegans
item.description: The nuclear hormone receptor NHR-49 regulates nutrition sensing and fatty acid metabolism in Caenorhabditis elegans . Here the authors show that NHR-49 activity in somatic cells regulates oocyte activation according to nutritional cues.

item.title: Nature Communications: Histone H4 lysine 20 tri-methylation safeguards breast cancer lineage fidelity and unfolded protein response
item.description: Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is highly heterogeneous, complicating treatment. Here, the authors show that the H4K20me3 heterochromatin mark regulates lineage identity and the unfolded protein response in TNBC and suggest KMT5B and KMT5C as therapeutic targets.

item.title: Nature Communications: The SIMDA framework maps PIP2-binding sites regulating the KCNQ1 channel
item.description: PIP2 lipid regulates the cardiac potassium channel KCNQ1. Here, the authors use multiscale simulations to map six PIP2 binding sites and show how KCNE3 and calmodulin redistribute lipid binding to tune channel activity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Nontoxic mRNA vehicles based on electrically neutral self-assembling peptides
item.description: Cationic and amphiphilic molecules often used in gene delivery can have toxic side effects. Here, the authors report on the co-assembly of electrically neutral self-assembling peptides and mRNA which produces highly biocompatible, nanotubular delivery vehicles with lower potential toxicity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Sex of central neurons controls intestinal niche signalling to drive sex differences in stem cell activity and cancer susceptibility
item.description: Sex hormones and cancer-cell sex influence tumor growth, but other sex-dependent drivers of oncogenesis remain unclear. Here, the authors reveal that the sex of central neurons alters the peripheral tumor-supportive niche to promote tumor growth.

item.title: Nature Communications: Constitutive natural killer cell features associated with post-treatment control of SIV infection in the pVISCONTI study
item.description: Early ART initiation enables durable HIV remission but the underlying immune mechanisms remain unclear. Here, Chapel, Romero-Martin and colleagues present evidence that constitutive NK cell features are associated with outcomes following ART interruption in cynomolgus macaques.

item.title: Nature Communications: Mapping of dynamic allostery within p38 alpha kinase via network analyses and NMR spectroscopy
item.description: Here, the authors apply dynamic network analysis, alongside a set of experimental validations, to probe correlated motions within p38α kinase. The data corroborate communication between its N- and C-lobes, including in particular the lipid pocket.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structure-guided allosteric modulation of the delta opioid receptor
item.description: In this study, authors report cryo-EM structures of the delta opioid receptor bound to a positive allosteric modulator, showing it forms a hydrogen bond that disrupts a conserved sodium-binding site, stabilizing the active receptor and guiding drug design.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genetic architecture of cytokine autoantibodies and associated risk of common diseases
item.description: Despite limited understanding of cytokine autoantibodies, this study reveals a heterogeneous genetic architecture, with distinct profiles conferring reduced risk of certain cancers and rheumatoid arthritis, but increased susceptibility to diabetes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Extracellular-matrix mediated stresses spatially bias myoblast fusion and myotube growth
item.description: Active self-organization of myoblasts, coupled with extracellular-matrix interactions, create mechanical stress patterns that bias cell fusion toward specific locations, providing a mechanistic link between tissue mechanics and muscle development.

item.title: Nature Communications: Data-driven construction of an imine reductase library capable of broad-scope reductive amination at equimolar substrate concentrations
item.description: Reductive amination catalysed by imine reductases and reductive aminases is a powerful method for the asymmetric synthesis of chiral amines, yet the generality and practical limitations of these enzymes remain poorly understood. Here, the authors combine large-scale, iterative activity screening, sequence analysis and machine-learning-guided exploration to profile reductive amination performance across 175 enzymes and structurally diverse substrate panels.

item.title: Nature Communications: CX3CR1⁺ CD8⁺ cytotoxic T cells drive tumor killing in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma during neoadjuvant therapy
item.description: Responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICI) in esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC) are highly heterogeneous, and the mechanisms underlying therapeutic sensitivity remain incompletely understood. Here the authors present multi-omics profiling of ESCC patients receiving neoadjuvant therapy and identify a CX3CR1⁺CD8⁺ T-cell cytotoxic effector state linked to response.

item.title: Nature Communications: Zanidatamab in patients with early stage HER2-positive breast cancer: the NeoZanHER phase 2 single-arm open-label trial
item.description: With the improvement of HER2-targeted therapy in patients with breast cancer, there is growing interest in whether chemotherapy can be eliminated from regimens completely. Here, the authors report a phase 2 clinical trial investigating neoadjuvant zanidatamab (HER2-targeting antibody) in patients with early-stage HER2-positive breast cancer.

item.title: Nature Communications: A case study of evolutionary variability and determinism among type III polyketide synthases
item.description: This study suggests that 3-oxo-glutaric acid-forming polyketide synthases evolved repeatedly from the intrinsic triacetic acid lactone-forming activity of chalcone synthases through independent, lineage-specific evolutionary events.

item.title: Nature Communications: Enhanced axonal mitochondrial motility and neural activity-induced energy deficits destabilize synaptic transmission in models of bipolar disorder
item.description: The contribution of mitochondrial trafficking and positioning to the disease mechanisms of bipolar disorder is unclear. Li et al. show that axonal mitochondrial hypermotility destabilizes presynaptic energy homeostasis, increasing synaptic variability in models of bipolar disorder that can be rescued by lithium treatment.

item.title: Nature Communications: Alcohol reshapes liver zonal plasticity and immune-metabolic reprogramming in metabolic-syndrome associated hepatocellular carcinoma
item.description: Alcohol consumption and high fat diet can drive liver cancer through distinct pathways. Here, the authors characterize three murine models of steatohepatitis-associated hepatocarcinogenesis that recapitulate metabolic dysfunction-associated steatohepatitis (MASH), alcohol-related liver disease (ALD), and their overlapped condition, MetALD, showing that alcohol reshapes liver zonal plasticity and β-catenin-AhR signaling to alter tumor origin and increase immunotherapy sensitivity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Compositional neurosymbolic representations enable efficient active exploration
item.description: Bayesian optimization can guide autonomous exploration but scales poorly, limiting its use on resource-constrained systems. Here, the authors introduce a neuro-symbolic embedding approach that delivers speedup, with partial implementation validated on neuromorphic hardware.

item.title: Nature Communications: Diversification in small mammals is associated with climatic specialisation, whereas species accumulation reflects evolutionary time
item.description: Why some lineages diversify explosively while others remain species-poor is been a central question in evolutionary biology. This global analysis on small mammals shows that climatic specialisation is associated with diversification whereas evolutionary time largely explains species accumulation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Divergent patterns of richness and density in the global soil seed bank
item.description: The soil seed bank is a vital aspect of biodiversity, helping plants to respond to changes in the environment. This global study shows that the number of seeds and species found in the soil depends on the specific contexts of the world’s ecosystems.

item.title: Nature Communications: An additional water is introduced into the manganese cluster during the formation of the S 3 state of photosystem II
item.description: Here, the authors report the S 3 state structure of Photosystem II solved with X-ray crystallography at two different energies using an XFEL. The results provide evidence for an oxygen ligand, O X (or O6) and do not support O-O bond formation in the S 3 state.

item.title: Nature Communications: Haemodynamic control of zonated liver function via instructive vascular Wnt signalling
item.description: The study identified blood flow as the key signal that programs liver blood vessels to instruct liver function through WNT signalling.

item.title: Nature Communications: Glucagon-like Peptide-1 Receptor Agonists and Risk of Tuberculosis in Type 2 Diabetes
item.description: A large international study found that certain diabetes drugs (GLP-1 receptor agonists) may link to a lower risk of tuberculosis than other common treatments. These medications may offer added protection against tuberculosis in type 2 diabetes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Longitudinal digital phenotyping of activity rhythms and biological aging using commercial wearables
item.description: Long-term links between free-living rest-activity rhythms and biological aging remain unclear. Here, the authors show that Fitbit-derived rest-activity rhythms are associated with biological aging trajectories in All of Us Research Program.

item.title: Nature Communications: Tirzepatide versus GLP-1 receptor agonists and stroke in patients with atrial fibrillation and type 2 diabetes
item.description: Among adults with atrial fibrillation and type 2 diabetes, tirzepatide use was associated with lower risks of stroke and death than other GLP-1 receptor agonists. The findings support trials of its cerebrovascular benefits in this high-risk group.

Nature Communications: 18 Month patency of acellular bioengineered regenerative conduit as coronary artery bypass
item.description: Here the authors tested lab-grown blood vessels as heart bypass grafts in sheep, adding an external support to prevent kinking. The vessels stayed open for 18 months, even after blood thinners were stopped, while transforming into living, functional tissue.

item.title: Nature Communications: Targeting ABL kinases overcomes melanoma immune evasion following resistance to MAPK inhibition
item.description: Although MAP kinase inhibitors (MAPKi) can initially reduce tumour burden in metastatic melanoma, resistance to treatment often occurs. Here, the authors demonstrate that concomitant treatment with ABL kinase inhibitors overcomes tumour resistance to MAPKi by promoting the accumulation of cytotoxic T lymphocytes and inhibiting the infiltration of immunosuppressive cells.

item.title: Nature Communications: Metabolic plasticity supports a flexible nutritional symbiosis in Cardiocondyla ants
item.description: Ancient symbioses may enable ants to thrive in diverse niches, but how these relationships are regulated remains unclear. This study reveals that some ants can dynamically regulate symbiont-derived benefits depending on the environmental context.

item.title: Nature Communications: CD11b agonist GB1275 potentiates oncolytic bacterial therapy against pancreatic cancer in mouse tumor models
item.description: Cancer immune therapy by oncolytic bacteria triggers immune cell activation against the tumors, but the therapeutic effect may be compromised by ant-bacterial immune activity. Here the authors combine oncolytic bacteria with a CD11b agonist that alters the composition of tumor-infiltrating myeloid cells in mouse models to favor anti-tumor innate activation while preventing clearance of the bacteria.

item.title: Nature Communications: Retroviruses use different IP 6 binding mechanisms to alter the properties of their capsids
item.description: Diverse retroviruses conserve IP 6 as a molecular glue for core assembly but use it differently: HIV-1 binds IP 6 within capsomer pores and needs it during virus production, while MPMV and MLV bind IP 6 between capsomers and require it during infection.

item.title: Nature Communications: YTHDC1 functions as a molecular chaperone to suppress ALS-linked hnRNPA1 mutants from aggregation
item.description: Researchers identify the RNA-binding protein YTHDC1 as an ATP-independent molecular chaperone that prevents harmful protein aggregation, revealing a link between RNA regulation and protein quality control in neurodegeneration.

item.title: Nature Communications: Fatty acid oxidation fuels mitochondrial respiration to drive epidermal stem cell fate and differentiation
item.description: How epidermal stem cells commit to differentiation remains incompletely understood. Here, the authors identify fatty acid oxidation as a key metabolic program that fuels mitochondrial energy production, enabling epidermal stem cells to initiate differentiation and sustain skin renewal.

item.title: Nature Communications: CFAP100 forms phase-separated condensates required for ciliary transition zone assembly
item.description: Here they identify CFAP100 as a critical regulator of ciliary transition zone assembly. Mechanistically, CFAP100 forms phase-separated condensates that promote transition zone organization, and recruits NPHP3 to facilitate ciliogenesis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Metabolic licensing of quiescent glioblastoma activation and immune evasion via astrocyte-mitochondria shuttle
item.description: Reactivation of quiescent cells at the invasive margin of glioblastoma tumors does not trigger an efficient immune elimination and these tumours tend to disseminate and recur even with therapy. Here the authors describe a metabolic regulatory pathway involving transfer of mitochondria enriched with the one‑carbon metabolism enzyme SHMT2, which cargo reactivates quiescent glioblastoma cells via metabolic regulation of mRNA methylation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Susceptibility of calves fed unpasteurized milk from cows infected with highly pathogenic avian influenza H5N1
item.description: In this study, the authors show that highly pathogenic avian influenza virus can be transmitted to calves fed unpasteurized milk from infected cows with infected calves showing clinical signs but that the presence of neutralizing antibodies in milk provides protection from infection.

item.title: Nature Communications: Native and introduced megafauna have convergent effects on animals and ecosystems: a meta-analysis
item.description: Megafauna are often assumed to have different ecological impacts depending on whether they are native or introduced. This global meta-analysis shows that both have broadly similar effects, suggesting that nativeness alone has limited power to predict ecological impacts.

item.title: Nature Communications: Astrocytes amplify cortical dopamine to encode winning memory in male mice
item.description: In this study, the authors find that initial victories activate D2 receptors in mPFC astrocytes, driving glutamate release and enhancing mPFC–NAc neuronal responses. This astrocytic mechanism consolidates winning memories and stabilizes social hierarchy in male mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structural and mechanistic insights into protective non-neutralizing antibodies targeting Crimean-Congo hemorrhagic fever virus nucleocapsid protein
item.description: This study identifies four antigenic sites on CCHFV NP, showing that protection is independent of head or stalk location. It maps the highly conserved binding epitope of mAb-9D5 in the head domain, enabling broad-spectrum efficacy and opening the door for effective combination therapies.

item.title: Nature Communications: Sex-specific trajectories of nonlinear immune aging at single-cell level
item.description: A multi-ethnic study of immune cells from 1,828 individuals finds that men and women age nonlinearly and differently at the cellular level. This work reveals sex-specific pathways and proposes personalized approaches to immune aging.

item.title: Nature Communications: TTC33 forms a complex with WDR61 and PHF5A to recruit factors relevant to genomic integrity
item.description: Authors identify the TANC complex, comprising TTC33, WDR61 and PHF5A, and show that it nucleates a protein interaction network containing factors implicated in splicing and DNA repair. Its disruption promotes genomic instability.

item.title: Nature Communications: A cuproptosis-inducing covalent organic framework synergizes with oncolytic virus for tumor radiotherapy
item.description: It has been reported that cuproptosis inducers can sensitize radioresistant tumors to radiotherapy (RT). Here, the authors report the synergistic anti-tumor efficacy of an oncolytic adenovirus combined with a radiation-responsive, copper-incorporated covalent organic framework, overcoming radio-resistance via induction of cuproptosis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Hypothalamic representation of aggressiveness across mouse strains
item.description: Genetics profoundly influences aggression by shaping neural circuits, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, authors show that strain differences in male mouse aggression are linked to differences in VMHvl neuron physiology.

item.title: Nature Communications: Lipopolysaccharide insertion and vesicle mediated turnover drive growth independent outer membrane adaptation in Escherichia coli
item.description: Lipopolysaccharide (LPS) organisation and turnover in E. coli is integral to outer membrane homeostasis. Here, pulse-chase labelling and imaging reveal sustained spatial segregation of pre-existing and newly inserted LPS, together with growth-independent LPS turnover by vesiculation.

item.title: Nature Communications: Experience-dependent changes in functional connectome fingerprinting
item.description: Researchers showed that shared military service temporarily reduces the distinctiveness of functional brain connectivity, lowering connectome fingerprinting accuracy while preserving individual stability and recovering over time.

item.title: Nature Communications: Motixafortide, cemiplimab, gemcitabine and nab-paclitaxel in metastatic pancreatic cancer: a single-arm phase 2 study with single-cell correlatives
item.description: The CXCR4-CXCL12 axis drives immune exclusion and immunosuppression in pancreatic cancer. Here, the authors report a single-arm phase 2 study of metastatic pancreatic cancer evaluating motixafortide (CXCR4 inhibitor), cemiplimab (PD-1 blockade) and chemotherapy, reporting a 64% response rate and 91% disease control, with CXCL12+ fibroblasts and T-cell changes linked to response.

item.title: Nature Communications: Acoustic cell patterning reveals geometry- and substrate-dependent vasculogenesis and human embryo model development
item.description: Here they describe a new cell patterning technique, acoustic cell patterning, which rapidly arranges multiple cell types on both soft and stiff surfaces to build vascular structures and human embryo models that exhibit characteristics not captured by existing methods.

item.title: Nature Communications: Six-compound cocktail for maturation of human pluripotent stem cell-derived liver spheroids for toxicity prediction
item.description: This study reports a defined cocktail that matures human iPSC-derived hepatocytes to transcriptionally and functionally mimic primary hepatocytes, enabling personalized drug toxicity prediction and recapitulation of key fatty liver disease features.

item.title: Nature Communications: Trimester-dependent vertical transmission of H5N1 influenza virus through placental and mammary routes impairs offspring development
item.description: Researchers found H5N1 bird flu can spread from pregnant mice to fetuses through the placenta and to newborns through milk, causing developmental delays, smaller size, and behavioral problems, highlighting pregnancy-related risks in mammals.

item.title: Nature Communications: HIPPIE: a generative model for electrophysiological analysis across species, technologies, and modalities
item.description: This presents HIPPIE, a deep-learning model that classifies neuron types from electrophysiological recordings across mice, rats and macaques, and can generate and translate signals between species or recording technologies.

item.title: Nature Communications: Directed evolution of an enantiocomplementary S N Arase reveals divergent catalytic features
item.description: Enzymes that catalyse non-natural C–C bond-forming reactions are of interest for asymmetric synthesis, but reprogramming their active sites to invert the stereochemical outcome remains challenging. Here, the authors report on the evolution of eS N Ar1.3 with inverted stereochemical outcome, enhanced activity and expanded substrate scope compared with S N Ar1.3, their previously engineered S N Arase.

item.title: Nature Communications: Molecular heterogeneity and clonal origin of CCR8 + effector regulatory T cells in human cancer
item.description: Studies of conserved molecular programs in regulatory T cells (Tregs) across human tumors are limited. Here, by integrating scRNAseq datasets from 9 tumor types, the authors identify a common signature of human Treg cells across solid tumors, further dissecting the molecular and functional heterogeneity of human intratumoral Tregs.

item.title: Nature Communications: Identification of a spatially organized TREM2-associated permissive macrophage niche in human pulmonary tuberculosis alveolar pneumonia
item.description: Pulmonary tuberculosis infection of the lung induces alveolar pneumonia and granulomas. Here, the authors analyze lung biopsies from four men with pulmonary tuberculosis, finding alveolar pneumonia to be enriched for TREM2 + macrophages, which are more susceptible for Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection than TREM2- macrophages.

item.title: Nature Communications: An endometrial immune atlas across the female menstrual cycle reveals lymphoid aggregates compromise pregnancy
item.description: The immune landscape of human endometrium is remodeled across the menstrual cycle. The authors here provide a comprehensive immune atlas of these changes, and show that ectopic lymphoid aggregates, composed of germinal-center-B-like cells and T follicular helper-like cells, form in mouse and human chronic endometritis, which might lead to adverse pregnancy outcomes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Deep learning for precision grading of Schistosoma japonicum -induced liver fibrosis in ultrasound images
item.description: Researchers developed a deep learning system that accurately grades schistosomiasis-related liver fibrosis from ultrasound, and deployed it on Windows and Android devices to support consistent screening and follow-up in endemic regions.

item.title: Nature Communications: Gestational age modifies associations between Group B Streptococcus genomic characteristics and postnatal age at disease onset
item.description: This Danish study shows that gestational age modifies the association between Group B Streptococcus genomic characteristics and postnatal age at disease onset in infants. The findings may help inform surveillance and maternal vaccination strategies.

item.title: Nature Communications: Plan-related inequalities in costs, disease progression and mortality among hypertensive patients in China
item.description: An analysis of 8 million hypertension-related hospital admissions in China shows that health insurance payment plans are linked to costs, disease progression and survival, revealing gaps in financial protection and access to care.

item.title: Nature Communications: Improving early prediction for adverse dengue outcomes using data from the IDAMS prospective multicentre study
item.description: Authors used laboratory tests and clinical symptoms to predict dengue progression in a multi-country study. Prediction models improved in accuracy over time, enabling earlier admission of high-risk patients without overwhelming hospital capacity.

item.title: Nature Communications: A systematic review and meta-analysis on heat thresholds for maternal health and birth outcomes
item.description: Pregnant individuals can be particularly vulnerable to environmental heat exposure. Here, the authors report a systematic review and meta-analysis that identifies temperature thresholds associated with increasing risks of adverse pregnancy and birth outcomes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Self-supervised image denoising and restoration method for atomic force microscopy
item.description: The authors present self-supervised Scanning Probe microscopy Image DEnoising and Restoration (SPIDER), a deep learning framework that denoises scanning probe microscopy images, enabling imaging acceleration and anisotropic resolution restoration.

item.title: Nature Communications: RNase-mediated defence and its association with SCC mec in Staphylococcus aureus
item.description: Antibiotic resistance in Staphylococcus aureus often emerges through acquisition of mobile genetic elements. Here, Kondo et al. identify an RNase-encoding gene that is present in methicillin-susceptible strains, but absent from resistant counterparts, and acts as a barrier to the uptake of mobile genetic elements.

item.title: Nature Communications: PubMind: literature-based genetic variant extraction and functional annotation using large language models
item.description: PubMind, an AI tool using large language models, extracts genetic variant–disease links and supporting evidence from millions of research papers, building a searchable database of ~1.3 million variants to advance precision medicine.

item.title: Nature Communications: Chromatin decompaction within the nucleus increases plasma membrane tension promoting NETosis execution, independently of transcription
item.description: Chromatin organizes nuclear DNA, but whether it actively regulates whole-cell mechanics remains unknown. Here, we used NETosis to show that chromatin decompaction within the nucleus increases plasma membrane tension and cell volume, establishing chromatin as a regulator of cell mechanics.

item.title: Nature Communications: Alternative tandem transcription initiation links noncoding variants to human disease through translational control
item.description: Alternative transcription initiation expands transcript diversity, but its contribution to disease is poorly understood. Here, the authors map genetic regulation of alternative transcription initiation across human tissues, revealing disease-associated genes and showing that many risk variants act through mechanisms undetected by traditional eQTL analyses.

item.title: Nature Communications: Scoop-shaped pores change how pollen is released from poricidal flowers
item.description: Poricidal flowers bear diverse pore shapes that influence pollen release, with scoop-shaped pores producing faster, narrower pollen streams. In buzz-pollination, different vibration frequencies reshape the pollen cloud, suggesting pollinator-specific complexity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Accelerating protein design by scaling experimental characterization
item.description: De novo protein design outpaces experimental validation. Here, authors present SAPP and DMX — scalable, semi-automated workflows enabling cloning, purification and characterization of hundreds to thousands of designed proteins per day at low cost.

item.title: Nature Communications: Hypoxia-activated scleraxis a mediates epicardial progenitor differentiation into a unique cardiac perivascular cell type
item.description: Here they identify a hypoxia-responsive pathway that directs epicardial progenitor cells into a new vessel-supporting cell type, uncovering a key mechanism by which the epicardium orchestrates heart development and regeneration.

item.title: Nature Communications: Humic acid’s sheltering effect paradoxically promotes antibiotic resistance gene dissemination during peroxymonosulfate water treatment
item.description: In this study, the authors show that humic acid, a common organic substance, shields bacteria from peroxymonosulfate disinfection, inadvertently promoting the spread of antibiotic resistance genes via natural transformation in aquatic environments.

item.title: Nature Communications: Temporal coding enables hyperacuity in event-based vision
item.description: Unlike conventional frame-based vision, biomimetic event-based sensing preserves precise temporal information. The authors show that these timing signals can be exploited to recover spatial details from tiny images, enabling event-based vision to outperform frame-based approaches.

item.title: Nature Communications: Epigenetic–epitranscriptomic crosstalk through TaHAG1–TaNSUN2 coordinates thermotolerance in wheat
item.description: High temperature can severely constrain crop productivity. Here the authors show that the mRNA m⁵C methyltransferase TaNSUN2 regulates thermotolerance in wheat and show that TaNSUN2 -overexpression can increase heat resilience.

item.title: Nature Communications: ALPaCA: Adapting Llama for Pathology Context Analysis to enable slide-level question answering
item.description: Large Vision Language Models (LVLMs) have revolutionised computational pathology, but still struggle with the analysis of pyramidal, gigapixel-scale whole-slide images (WSIs). Here, the authors introduce ALPaCA (Adapting Llama for Pathology Context Analysis), a general-purpose slide-level LVLM designed for WSI analysis and question answering across a broad range of cancer types and tissue sites.

item.title: Nature Communications: Drug screen and machine learning predict neuroprotective agents in a preclinical human model of childhood dementia
item.description: Here authors show patient-derived neural models of childhood dementia exhibit key disease features. A drug screening platform integrating machine learning, imaging, transcriptomics and electrophysiology, identifies repurposed compounds that mitigate adverse effects.

item.title: Nature Communications: Citrate synthase condensation requires catalytic events in Corynebacterium glutamicum
item.description: The molecular mechanisms underlying protein condensation remain poorly understood. Here the authors discover and characterise the dynamic condensation of citrate synthase in C. glutamicum , showing condensation is dependent on catalytic activity and substrate binding.

item.title: Nature Communications: Crosstalk between S -nitrosylation and glycation defines a metabolic vulnerability in liver and renal cancers
item.description: Aldo-ketoreductase 1A1 (AKR1A1), a detoxifying enzyme, is reported to have an alternative role in regulating S-nitrosylation. Here, the authors show that AKR1A1 regulates S-nitrosylation of PKM2, and its loss leads to metabolic changes that promote chemoresistance and cell migration in liver and renal cancers.

item.title: Nature Communications: Clonal sharing and plasticity of follicular CD4 + T cells across lymph nodes and tumors in non-small cell lung cancer
item.description: To provide additional insights into the biology of CD4 + T cells in cancer, here the authors report a multi-omics analysis of CD4 + T cells from matched blood, tumor invaded lymph nodes (LNs), and tumor tissues of patients with non-small cell lung cancer, showing that tumor-invaded LNs and tumors harbor clonally linked and plastic follicular CD4+T cell subsets.

item.title: Nature Communications: Metalloimmunological hydrogel-based cancer vaccine potentiates postoperative tumor immunotherapy
item.description: Adjuvant immune checkpoint inhibitor (AICI) therapy is promising but suffers from inadequate durable immunological memory against tumor recurrence and metastasis. Here this group design a metalloimmunological hydrogel-based cancer vaccine that synergizes innate-adaptive crosstalk to potentiate AICI efficacy.

item.title: Nature Communications: Decoding isozyme-specific substrate recognition in protein arginine deiminases by in vitro lysate-based citrullination mapping
item.description: Protein citrullination by PAD enzymes is vital for cell function but isozyme specificity is poorly understood. Here, the authors map thousands of in vitro modification sites across the active human PAD family to reveal the landscape and structural rules governing substrate recognition.

item.title: Nature Communications: Rivers of salt: the extent of salinization in European running waters
item.description: A continent-wide study finds river salinity far above natural baseline levels across Europe. Many waterways exceed safety limits for wildlife, drinking water, and irrigation, pointing to a need for EU-wide salinization standards.

item.title: Nature Communications: Blood-brain barrier-penetrant nanotherapy inhibits haem oxygenase-1-mediated ferroptosis for post-resuscitation neuroprotection
item.description: Limited drug delivery across the blood-brain barrier (BBB) hinders the therapy of post-resuscitation brain injury after cardiac arrest. Here, the authors report zwitterionic poly (tertiary amine oxide)-based micelles that cross the BBB via transcytosis and deliver artesunate to suppress haem oxygenase-1-driven ferroptosis, restore iron homeostasis and provide neuroprotection after resuscitation.

item.title: Nature Communications: The DLX/Notch axis is necessary for spatiotemporal regulation of neural cell fate
item.description: Neural stem cells adopt one of three major cell fates during embryonic development. Here, DLX2 is shown to suppress glial fate through direct transcriptional regulation, uncovering distinct mechanisms that are essential for neuronal specification

item.title: Nature Communications: CoxFormer enables spatial omics inference with multimodal generative modeling
item.description: Yang, Liao, Zhang and colleagues present CoxFormer, an approach that learns whole-transcriptome gene representations from biomedical knowledge and co-expression data, thereby enabling spatial omics to predict unmeasured genes, enhance resolution and identify disease-related tissue regions.

item.title: Nature Communications: Structure-guided identification of denitrification inhibitors to mitigate agricultural N 2 O emissions
item.description: A key gap in agricultural climate mitigation is the lack of interventions that specifically target denitrification. This study identifies that triazole compounds act as cytochrome P450 inhibitors, effectively reducing N₂O emissions from denitrification.

item.title: Nature Communications: Interface-engineered iron single-atom biohybrids for efficient CO 2 -to-bioplastic conversion
item.description: The integration of inorganic–microbial systems offers promise for CO 2 -to-chemical conversion but faces efficiency bottlenecks. Here, the authors report an engineering strategy of anchoring iron single-atom catalysts onto bacterial membranes to achieve enhanced bioplastic production.

item.title: Nature Communications: Diagnostic performance and antibiotic impact of droplet digital PCR in suspected sepsis: the PROGRESS trial
item.description: In a multicenter randomized trial of patients with suspected sepsis, droplet digital PCR identified bloodstream pathogens faster and more often than blood culture and guided earlier, better-targeted antibiotics linked to improved survival.

item.title: Nature Communications: Shape-independent fluidity in epithelial cell monolayers
item.description: Researchers demonstrate that weakening cell-cell adhesion increases epithelial tissue fluidity without altering cell shape, revealing that dissipative mechanics are a previously unrecognized factor controlling collective tissue behavior.

item.title: Nature Communications: Surface-water carbon exchange from mangroves and responses to global warming
item.description: Surface-water carbon export from mangroves averages 101 mmol m⁻² d⁻¹. Warming scenarios project exports increasing up to 305% until ~2.5 °C threshold, then declining. This lateral flux represents a major, overlooked carbon sequestration pathway.

item.title: Nature Communications: AI-enabled discovery and biochemical optimization of minibinders targeting cancer cell-surface proteins
item.description: In this work the authors present a scalable mammalian cell-display workflow to identify AI-designed minibinders against cancer surface targets. AI-guided optimization beyond the binding interface improves their expression as chimeric antigen receptors and target-selective killing.

item.title: Nature Communications: Atomic structure and plasticity of the CTX-MthK complex investigated by cryo-EM, NMR, and MD simulations
item.description: Cryo-EM, NMR, and MD simulations reveal how charybdotoxin (CTX) binds to the MthK potassium channel, identifying key residues that stabilize toxin binding and block potassium ion conduction

item.title: Nature Communications: Structural origins of species-specific differences in TRPV2 activation
item.description: This study reveals why human and rodent TRPV2 ion channels respond differently to heat and chemicals. Using electrophysiology and cryo-EM, the authors identify structural changes and key residues that tune species-specific TRPV2 activation.

item.title: Nature Communications: ibSLS as a biobank for democratizing access to multi-omics data and biospecimens from spaceflight research
item.description: To enable spaceflight biology data to be easier to find, explore, and use, this study introduces ibSLS, a platform for visualizing multi-omics data from Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency mouse spaceflight missions.

item.title: Nature Communications: Semi-supervised Omics Factor Analysis (SOFA) disentangles known and latent sources of variation in multi-omic data
item.description: Capraz et al. introduce Semi-supervised Omics Factor Analysis (SOFA), a computational framework for multi-omics analysis. SOFA disentangles known from novel variation, and infers latent factors that give insights into diverse biological processes.

item.title: Nature Communications: Bispecific chimeric autoantibody receptor T cells eliminate acetylcholine receptor-specific B cells in myasthenia gravis models
item.description: Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune neuromuscular disorder mediated by autoantibodies targeting the nicotinic acetylcholine receptor. Here, the authors engineered chimaeric autoantibody receptor T cells that reduced pathogenic autoantibody titres and IgG deposition in a mouse model.

item.title: Nature Communications: Impact of the anti-inflammatory macrolide glasmacinal on the gut microbiota of healthy adults: an open-label trial
item.description: Here, in a clinical trial in healthy participants, the authors show that glasmacinal, an oral macrolide with immunomodulatory properties, exerts limited changes to the gut microbiome and does select for antimicrobial resistance, unlike conventional antibiotics.

item.title: Nature Communications: Advancing human-centric AI for robust X-ray analysis through holistic self-supervised learning
item.description: In this study, Moutakanni and colleagues introduce RayDINO, a self-supervised chest X-ray foundation model trained on 840,000 images, that outperforms supervised methods across nine radiology tasks and shows improved generalization and reduced bias across demographics.

item.title: Nature Communications: Associations of loneliness, social isolation and healthy lifestyle with life expectancy free of major physical disease and mental disorder
item.description: The authors observe that loneliness and social isolation relate to shorter life expectancy free of physical (type 2 diabetes, cardiovascular disease, chronic respiratory disease, neurodegenerative disease, and cancer) and mental disorders (depression and anxiety) in the UK Biobank. These associations are particularly pronounced for mental disorders, and the loss of disease-free life expectancy associated with social isolation is attenuated in individuals with healthier lifestyles.

Nature Communications: Sensorimotor remapping drives task specialization in prefrontal cortex
item.description: How the prefrontal cortex support flexible behavior across different tasks remains unclear. Here, the authors show that sensorimotor remapping drives task-specialized neuronal populations and that varying degrees of specialization can be explained by network modulations.

item.title: Nature Communications: Long-read proteogenomic atlas of human neuronal differentiation reveals isoform diversity informing neurodevelopmental risk mechanisms
item.description: Alternative splicing expands neuronal diversity, but many brain RNA isoforms remain uncharacterized. Here, the authors generate a high‑resolution proteogenomic atlas of human neuron development, uncovering thousands of novel isoforms and revealing dynamic splicing changes in autism risk genes.

item.title: Nature Communications: STADiffuser: high-fidelity simulation and full-view 3D modeling of spatial transcriptomics
item.description: Zhang and Zhang present STADiffuser, a computational framework for high-fidelity simulation of spatial transcriptomics data and for full-view 3D tissue modeling from limited spatial measurements.

item.title: Nature Communications: HMGA1-HP1β axis regulates premature aging in Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome through chromatin remodeling
item.description: Premature aging disorders and normal aging involve changes in chromatin, but the key regulators are not fully understood. Here, the authors show HMGA1 stabilizes HP1β to remodel chromatin, curb cellular aging and extend lifespan in a progeria mouse model.

item.title: Nature Communications: CK2α restriction of STING accumulation underlies systemic aging
item.description: Lamin A/C scaffolds STING and CK2α at the nuclear periphery, promoting STING phosphorylation and turnover to reduce cGAS-STING-driven inflammaging, and this LMNA–CK2–STING axis curbs senescence in myeloid cells and systemic aging.

item.title: Nature Communications: A multicenter kidney transplantation study identifies hierarchy and directionality of HLA-DQ alloimmune responses
item.description: Antibody mediated rejection is a main cause of graft rejection in organ transplantation and is often seen as de-novo donor specific antibodies (dnDSA) targeting the donor’s mismatched HLA-DQ molecules. Here the authors use a multi-center cohort to characterise HLA-DQ mismatches in kidney allograft recipients showing hierarchy in generation of dnDSA and antibody mediated rejection and application of these qualitative measures in alloimmune risk stratification.

item.title: Nature Communications: Transcriptional activity during seed imbibition is conserved, robust and required for germination
item.description: Seeds are known to accumulate mRNA, and it has been suggested that they do not need Pol II transcription early in germination. Here the authors show that new mRNA synthesis starts shortly after water absorption and is crucial for seed germination.

item.title: Nature Communications: APOE genotypes differentially remodel the astrocytic lipid droplet proteome to shape lipid droplet dynamics
item.description: Alzheimer’s-linked APOE variants affect the composition and plasticity of astrocytic lipid droplets. These fat storage organelles are rapidly turned over with protective APOE2 , but clear slowly with Alzheimer's-associated APOE4 .

item.title: Nature Communications: Plasma proteomics defines two reproducible subphenotypes of sepsis-associated acute kidney injury with distinct outcomes
item.description: Sepsis is a leading cause of acute kidney injury in critically ill patients and carries a high risk of death, yet its biology varies between patients. Here, the authors show that plasma proteomics defines two subtypes with distinct outcomes and drug response, identified by a seven-protein test.

item.title: Nature Communications: Modelling anti-Ov16 seroprevalence for the control and elimination of onchocerciasis
item.description: Ov16 antibody tests are used for onchocerciasis surveillance. Fitting a transmission model to age-stratified seroprevalence data identified patent infection as the most likely parasite stage leading to seropositivity, indicating ongoing transmission.

item.title: Nature Communications: Locus-specific stratification and prioritization unveil genetic risk mechanism underlying complex diseases
item.description: Genetic risk of complex diseases poses unique challenges. Here, the authors develop a locus-specific stratification and gene regulatory prioritisation strategy to address issues arising from multi-signals in complex diseases.

item.title: Nature Communications: Global genomic surveillance uncovers emergence and spatiotemporal patterns of World Health Organization priority antibiotic resistance in invasive Salmonella
item.description: Antimicrobial resistance in invasive Salmonella is an escalating global health threat, yet its global trends and genomic evidence remain poorly understood. Wang and Xu et al . use a state-of-the-art pipeline integrating global genomics to reveal emergence and spatiotemporal patterns of WHO priority antibiotic resistance in invasive Salmonella .

item.title: Nature Communications: Tracking funding disparities in global health aid with machine learning
item.description: Misalignment between health aid and country-level disease burden can leave populations without the necessary support for major health challenges. Here the authors report a machine learning analysis of global health aid and conclude that aid is often misaligned with country-level disease burden, with non-communicable diseases receiving limited aid despite their large global burden.

item.title: Nature Communications: Measurable residual disease detected by next-generation sequencing in T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia
item.description: The clinical value of next-generation sequencing for measurable residual disease (NGS-MRD) monitoring in T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia remains to be fully established. Tracking TCR rearrangements in pediatric patients, this study shows that NGS-MRD serves as a useful method to stratify outcomes and identifies high-risk cases.

item.title: Nature Communications: Engineered bacteria as exogenous organelle mimics restore PTEN and p53 tumor suppressor functions for cancer therapy
item.description: PTEN and p53 are two of the most frequently mutated or inactivated tumor suppressor genes. Here, the authors engineer Salmonella to act as exogenous organelle-like devices that deliver PTEN and an MDM2 inhibitor to reactivate p53 to tumors, achieving durable tumor suppression and synergistic immune activation.

item.title: Nature Communications: A viral-based individualized neoantigen vaccine as adjuvant treatment in resected head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: a randomized Phase I trial
item.description: Patients with head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC) have limited sensitivity to immunotherapies. The authors report the development of TG4050, a modified vaccinia Ankara (MVA) virus-based individualized neoantigen vaccine, here tested in a randomized phase I trial as adjuvant treatment in patients with resected HNSCC.

item.title: Nature Communications: Intracellular artificial DNA receptor-loaded gelated cells for aflatoxin theranostics
item.description: The mycotoxin Aflatoxin B1 is highly toxic to human beings. Here, Li and co-workers report that engineered cell particles carrying aflatoxin aptamers can be used to both detect and eliminate Aflatoxin B1, in vitro and in vivo.

item.title: Nature Communications: PD-1 regulates CD4 + T cell-mediated CD8 + T cell responses in the brain to balance viral control and neuroinflammation
item.description: JC polyomavirus infection can result in progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy, and T cells have been shown to express PD-1. Here the authors show that PD-1 regulates the CD4 + T cell mediated CD8 + T cell response in the brain regulating the antiviral response and neuroinflammation in a mouse polyomavirus central nervous system infection model.

item.title: Nature Communications: Sintilimab plus Bevacizumab biosimilar IBI305 and chemotherapy as a first-line treatment in advanced gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma (SBAGA): a single-arm, phase Ib/II study
item.description: Previous evaluations on anti-VEGF monoclonal antibody indicate its therapeutic potential in gastric cancer treatment. Here this group reports a phase Ib/II trial combining sintilimab/bevacizumab biosimilar IBI305/CapeOX chemotherapy as the first-line treatment on 54 patients with HER2-negative advanced gastric or gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma.

item.title: Nature Communications: CD36-mediated lipid-accumulation in reactive microglia contributes to retinal degeneration via the NLRP3-IL-1β pathway in mice
item.description: Metabolic stress can reshape immune cells into drivers of tissue damage. This study identifies CD36-driven lipid accumulation in reactive microglia as a mechanism linking retinal inflammation to degeneration.

item.title: Nature Communications: Bidirectional associations between loneliness and physical multimorbidity and the mediating role of social inactivity
item.description: Both multimorbidity and loneliness are major public health issues. Here, the authors show that physical multimorbidity and loneliness are bidirectionally linked and social inactivity partially mediates the pathway from physical multimorbidity to loneliness.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genome-wide pQTL mapping in human skin identifies specific genetic regulators and mechanistic links to skin disorders
item.description: This study creates a genetic map of protein regulation in human skin, identifying genetic regulators of protein abundance and candidate disease-related proteins linked to leprosy, atopic dermatitis and psoriasis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Phosphorylation of OTUB1 promotes autophagy initiation under starvation
item.description: This study uncovers a phosphorylation-dependent regulatory mechanism controlling OTUB1’s function in nutrient deficiency-triggered autophagy initiation, providing cellular and molecular evidence supporting the therapeutic potential of fasting in alleviating MASLD.

item.title: Nature Communications: In vivo labeling–based proteomic analysis of early follicle oocytes and cisplatin-induced alterations in mice
item.description: Using in situ APEX labeling, this study maps proteins and RNA in mouse oocytes from early ovarian follicles and shows how cisplatin alters these cells, identifying EZH2 inhibition as a potential strategy to lessen cisplatin-induced oocyte damage.

item.title: Nature Communications: DUSP4 promotes anti-tumor CD8 + T cell function and boosts CAR-T cell efficacy in mouse colorectal cancer
item.description: Dual-specificity phosphatases (DUSPs) regulate cellular signaling pathways by dephosphorylating protein residues, which also modulates CD8 + T cell signaling. Here, the authors investigate the role of DUSP4 in AOM/DSS-induced colorectal cancer, finding DUSP4 to enhance T cell-mediated anti-tumor immunity via ERK2-KLF2 signaling.

item.title: Nature Communications: Safety and immunogenicity of inactivated human Rotavirus vaccine in young children and infants: a randomized, placebo-controlled, double-blind, phase I clinical trial
item.description: This double-blind, randomized, placebo-controlled, dose escalation phase I trial evaluates the safety and immunogenicity of an inactivated rotavirus vaccine (IRV) in healthy young children and infants without prior rotavirus vaccination or HIV infection.

item.title: Nature Communications: Tubular ACSM3 controls fatty acid metabolism and safeguards against acute kidney injury in male mice
item.description: Fatty acid oxidation impairment represents a hallmark of acute kidney injury (AKI). Here the authors report that tubular deficiency of ACSM3, an enzyme involved in medium chain fatty acid activation, is protective against kidney injury in male mouse models of AKI potentially via modulating PPARα activity.

item.title: Nature Communications: AAT/ SERPINA1 Pi*Z variant linked to gestational length and preterm birth prevention via AAT in mice
item.description: Preterm birth affects around 10% of pregnancies and lacks effective preventive therapies. Here, the authors identify the SERPINA1 PiZ variant as a genetic risk factor for shorter gestational duration and show that alpha‑1‑antitrypsin supplementation protects against inflammation‑induced preterm birth in mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multi-ancestry genetic architecture of heart failure subtypes
item.description: This study maps the genetic basis of major heart failure subtypes across diverse populations, identifying shared and subtype-specific risk variants that may inform biology, risk prediction and future therapies.

item.title: Nature Communications: Commensal bacteria inhibit viral infections via a tryptophan metabolite
item.description: Previous studies suggest that commensal bacteria modulate viral infections. Here, the authors use HIV as a model to show that commensal bacteria impact viral infections, pinpointing a specific tryptophan metabolite as a key player.

item.title: Nature Communications: Amiloride mitigates respiratory distress caused by WFDC2 deficiency via inhibiting the epithelial sodium channel
item.description: This study identifies a WFDC2 mutation that causes a severe cystic-fibrosis-like airway disease in humans and mice. The mutation overactivates the epithelial sodium channel, and treatment with the drug amiloride improves survival and lung function in affected mice.

item.title: Nature Communications: A foundation model for acute abdomen diagnosis stratification and triage on noncontrast computed tomography
item.description: The authors present AbdomenNet, a foundation model for non-contrast computed tomography. It detects 11 acute abdominal conditions, helps identify high-risk cases, improves radiologist accuracy, and may speed emergency reporting.

item.title: Nature Communications: Large-scale admixture mapping in the All of Us Research Program improves the characterization of cross-population phenotypic differences
item.description: In this work, Mandla et al. identified >50 genetic loci where ancestry was associated with a trait, expanding on the underlying biological mechanisms of these traits and the potential genetic factors of their differences between populations.

item.title: Nature Communications: IL-2 mutein-engrafted antibody MHS552 selectively expands functional regulatory T cells in nonclinical models and healthy participants
item.description: Although low-dose IL-2 therapy has shown promise in treating autoimmune and inflammatory conditions by supporting the expansion and immunosuppressive activity of regulatory T cells (Treg), robust clinical responses have been lacking. Here, the authors describe the design of the Treg-selective IL-2 agonist MHS552, its preclinical characterization in non-human primates, and a first-in-human dose escalation study in healthy participants reporting efficacy, selectivity and safety of the IL-2 mutein.

item.title: Nature Communications: Population-based genomic detection of childhood cancer predisposition using newborn dried blood spots
item.description: Prospective genomic newborn screening in large populations with extended follow-ups are necessary to assess the impact of the inclusion of cancer genes on outcomes. Here, the authors show that newborn screening for germline cancer risk, using a limited panel of cancer predisposition genes, would identify the approximately 1/27,000 babies who will develop a cancer in the first eight years of life due to a cancer predisposition syndrome, including nearly all children who go on to develop bilateral retinoblastoma.

item.title: Nature Communications: Neutrophil extracellular traps promote liver metastasis by impairing NK cell-dependent tumor surveillance via CCDC25
item.description: The formation of neutrophil extracellular traps (NETs) contributes to liver metastasis and immune suppression. Here the authors show that NET-derived DNA can be sensed by CCDC25 on natural killer (NK) cells impairing NK cell-dependent tumor surveillance and promoting liver metastasis.

item.title: Nature Communications: Chronic conditions and aortic disease risk: a prospective cohort study with predictive and etiological analyses
item.description: This study shows that multimorbidity and several chronic conditions, including cardiovascular, respiratory and kidney diseases, are associated with higher risk of aortic disease in two large cohorts.

item.title: Nature Communications: Noninvasive 3D mapping of tissue stress using reverberant shear wave
item.description: Mechanical stress shapes soft tissue health, but imaging it non-invasively in vivo has remained a challenge. Here, authors used physics-informed MRI wave analysis to map 3D tissue stress, enabling non-invasive intracranial pressure and tumor-induced stress estimates in brain tumor patients.

item.title: Nature Communications: Th17 effector cytokines induce shared and distinct microglial and endothelial cell responses in a mouse model for post-streptococcal encephalitis
item.description: Group A Streptococcus (GAS) infections can cause neuropsychiatric symptoms in children, but the underlying mechanisms remain unclear. Here, the authors show that IL-17A–IL17RA signaling in microglia mediates blood brain barrier dysfunction and neuroinflammation after GAS infection in a mouse model.

item.title: Nature Communications: Blood metabolomic signatures linking air pollution to lung cancer in the Cancer Prevention Studies
item.description: Exposure to ambient air pollution is an established risk factor for lung cancer. In here, the authors report multiple metabolic perturbations that may mediate the association between ambient air pollution exposure and lung cancer risk.

item.title: Nature Communications: Pseudomonas aeruginosa -derived volatile organic compounds modulate AhR signaling to dysregulate airway mucus homeostasis
item.description: Volatile organic compounds (VOCs) produced by Pseudomonas aeruginosa are potential biomarkers for diagnosing acute exacerbation in diseased lungs. Kuo et al. reveal that VOCs activate the aryl hydrocarbon receptor to exacerbate airway mucus pathology.

item.title: Nature Communications: Evidence of dengue transmission and a diverse Aedes mosquito virome on the Congo’s Angola border
item.description: Mosquito sequencing along the DRC-Angola border reveals diverse viruses and evidence of ongoing dengue transmission. This study shows that xenosurveillance has the potential to improve emerging infectious disease detection and prevention.

item.title: Nature Communications: Adaptive oncogenesis of β-catenin emerges from declining liver tissue integrity
item.description: Despite being a common driver of hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), oncogenic β-catenin is ineffective at initiating liver cancer on its own. Here the authors show that β-catenin mutations as a single genetic event confer negative fitness in the healthy liver, while driving clonal expansion and tumorigenesis as liver tissue integrity declines with chronic liver disease or aging.

item.title: Nature Communications: Clinical utility of molecular residual disease detection in early-stage resected EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer
item.description: For patients with resected EGFR-mutated lung cancer, effective strategies to guide post-surgical surveillance remain an unmet need. Here, the author shows that a personalized blood test may indicate molecular residual disease months before radiological progression.

item.title: Nature Communications: MRICombo: a deep-learning-based framework for universal volumetric segmentation grading-staging and malignancy detection across heterogeneous MRI
item.description: Existing magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) deep learning models are often task- or sequence-specific. Here, the authors present MRICombo, which segments anatomy, labels tumor types, and supports grading, staging and malignancy detection across heterogeneous sequences.

item.title: Nature Communications: Targeting m 6 A writer METTL3 with engineered nanovesicles reduces neuroinflammation in vitro and in vivo
item.description: Strategies to modulate neuroinflammation have broad therapeutic potential. Here, the authors develop siMETTL3-hNVs, nanovesicles carrying siRNA targeting METTL3, and show they can reduce neuroinflammation in vitro and in vivo.

item.title: Nature Communications: Diet-responsive proteogenomic effects following short-term restriction of animal products in humans
item.description: Using longitudinal proteogenomics, the authors reveal diet- and season-sensitive genetic effects on protein abundance linked to cholesterol and methionine metabolism and to immune function.

item.title: Nature Communications: Uncovering the signaling networks of disseminated glioblastoma cells in vivo with INSIGHT
item.description: Glioblastoma recurrence is driven by rare tumor cells that disseminate into the brain, but their signaling programs in vivo are poorly defined. Here, authors develop INSIGHT to map cell-type-specific signaling networks and show that disseminated cells rewire signaling network and global kinase activity toward neuronal and invasion associated pathways.

item.title: Nature Communications: Pan-Ebolavirus nanoparticle vaccine provides protection in rodents from lethal infection by Zaire and Sudan viruses
item.description: This study describes the design and structural characterization of two-component self-assembling nanoparticles co-displaying prefusion Zaire ebolavirus (EBOV) and Sudan ebolavirus (SUDV) glycoprotein antigens with protective capacity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Discovery of a peripheral Myh11-expressing nucleus pulposus cell population demontrating therapeutic potential for disc degeneration
item.description: The authors identify Myh11+ nucleus pulposus cells that maintain disc health throughout life. Their loss accelerates degeneration, while targeting or transplanting them protects, offering a promising regenerative strategy for spinal disorders.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multi-population GWAS meta-analysis identifies bladder cancer susceptibility loci and highlights genetic regulation of smoking-related risk
item.description: This study integrates genetic data from diverse populations to identify 70 loci linked to bladder cancer risk, including 43 novel, and uses experimental approaches to uncover how inherited variation influences this risk in the context of smoking.

item.title: Nature Communications: Healthy vaccinee effect in the evaluation of updated COVID-19 vaccines in elderly populations
item.description: This Swedish population study reveals that healthy vaccinee bias inflates estimates of the effectiveness of updated COVID-19 vaccines in adults aged 65 years or older, highlighting the need to account for frailty and overall health status.

item.title: Nature Communications: Standardized chronic disease management reduces comorbidity risk in China
item.description: Using linked health and medical records from 26 million residents in Shenzhen, China, the authors show that enrollment in the national Chronic Disease Patient Management program is associated with lower comorbidity risk among patients newly diagnosed with hypertension or type 2 diabetes.

item.title: Nature Communications: The efficacy, immunogenicity and safety of the LZ901 vaccine for herpes zoster virus in adults 40 years of age or older: a multicentre, randomised, double-blind, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial
item.description: Jingxin Li and colleagues report a randomized, placebo-controlled, phase 3 trial to evaluate the efficacy and safety of LZ901, recombinant gE-Fc fusion protein adjuvanted with aluminium hydroxide, against herpes zoster. They report that the vaccine reduces the risk of viral infection and has favorable safety profiles.

item.title: Nature Communications: CAFs shape the immunosuppressive microenvironment of pancreatic cancer through the Lin28b-STING Axis
item.description: Lin28b is an RNA-binding protein associated with cell transformation and human malignancies. Here, the authors show that Lin28b+ CAFs promote an immunosuppressive microenvironment in pancreatic cancer via inhibition of cGAS-STING signaling.

item.title: Nature Communications: Vulnerability to climate-driven pathogen-specific diarrheal diseases: secondary analysis from the Global Enteric Multicenter Study and Vaccine Impact on Diarrhea in Africa follow-up
item.description: Across the three African countries of The Gambia, Kenya and Mali, Kowalcyk et al identify socio-demographic factors that may mitigate the risks of climate drivers on pathogen-specific diarrheal diseases in young children.

item.title: Nature Communications: PPARα activation overcomes fibroinflammatory liver microenvironment-associated anti-PD-1 resistance in hepatocellular carcinoma by mediating GSDME-dependent pyroptosis
item.description: A fibroinflammatory liver microenvironment (FILM) is prevalent in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) and associated with anti-PD-1 resistance. Here the authors show that FILM suppresses GSDME-dependent pyroptosis and drives immune suppression, proposing PPARα activation as a strategy to overcome FILM-associated immune resistance in HCC.

item.title: Nature Communications: MBNL depletion drives stem cell fusion and immature myonuclear states in myotonic dystrophy type 1
item.description: This study shows that muscle stem cells fuse with existing muscle fibres in myotonic dystrophy type 1, producing centrally located nuclei with altered gene-expression states and reshaping diseased muscle.

item.title: Nature Communications: Diagnostic performance of plasma pTau217 in genetically admixed South American populations
item.description: Martino-Adami et al. show that plasma pTau217 accurately identifies Alzheimer’s disease pathology and aligns with clinical diagnosis in admixed South American cohorts, supporting its use where access to cerebrospinal fluid testing is limited.

item.title: Nature Communications: Chrono-atlas of cell-type specific daily gene expression rhythms in the regenerating colon
item.description: How tissues maintain circadian rhythms during regeneration remains poorly understood. Here, the authors generate a 24-hour single-cell transcriptomic atlas of the regenerating mouse colon and show that cells dynamically adapt their circadian programs in a cell-, region-, and injury-dependent manner.

item.title: Nature Communications: Ribosomal architecture and rRNA modification landscape in the tick-borne parasite Babesia divergens
item.description: Babesia microti and B. divergens are tick-borne parasites that are the most prevalent causes of human babesiosis. Here, the authors present cryo-EM structures of ribosomes from B. divergens . Nanopore sequencing reveals distinct rRNA modifications.

item.title: Nature Communications: A critical role of the histone lysine demethylase JmjC1 in regulating severe malaria-associated virulence genes in Plasmodium falciparum
item.description: Severe malaria is linked to upsA var gene expression, whose regulation remains unclear. Here, the authors identify JmjC1 as an epigenetic regulator of upsA var genes at the transcriptional level through chromatin and nuclear organization.

item.title: Nature Communications: α-Synuclein blocks endoplasmic reticulum co-translational protein translocation early in Parkinson’s disease
item.description: Proteomic and transcriptomic profiling on hiPSC-derived midbrain dopaminergic neurons with pathological α-synuclein burden reveals defective Sec61A interactions and co-translational translocation of ER-processed proteins.

item.title: Nature Communications: p38β-mediated BiP phosphorylation drives stemness and chemoresistance by suppressing UPR activation in hepatocellular carcinoma
item.description: Tumor-initiating cells drive chemoresistance in hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). Here, the authors discover that p38β/MAPK11 phosphorylation of BiP promotes stemness and chemoresistance in HCC.

item.title: Nature Communications: Single-nucleus analysis of human white adipose tissue reveals adipocyte subsets with distinct metabolic profiles
item.description: Single-nucleus profiling of human adipose tissue reveals low-maturation adipocyte subtypes with pro-inflammatory and pro-fibrotic signatures linked to metabolic disease and identifies TSHZ3 as a regulator of adipogenesis

item.title: Nature Communications: Non-invasive characterization of perivascular subarachnoid spaces
item.description: Cerebrospinal fluid’s compartmentalization remains unclear. Here, the authors show increased CSF-mobility around major cerebral arteries within the surrounding subarachnoid space, suggesting the presence of distinct CSF spaces in healthy individuals.

item.title: Nature Communications: Vitamin B5 supports anti-PD1 response in HER2-positive gastric cancer and enhances interaction between naïve B cells and T cells
item.description: HER2 + gastric cancer (GC) is commonly treated with immune checkpoint blockade. Here, the authors propose vitamin B5 as potential contributor to naïve B cell function in anti-PD-1-treated GC, finding B5 to be reduced in non-responders and B5 supplementation to improve anti-PD-1 response in a subcutaneous cancer mouse model.

item.title: Nature Communications: Pregnancy promotes tumor metastasis through adenosine-induced immunosuppressive neutrophils in pre-metastatic microenvironment
item.description: Accelerated cancer progression during pregnancy has been previously reported. Here the authors show that adenosine produced in the uterus of pregnant mice promotes tumor metastasis by favouring the accumulation of immunosuppressive neutrophils in the pre metastatic microenvironment.

item.title: Nature Communications: A second yearly booster dose of the VLA15 Lyme borreliosis vaccine candidate in healthy individuals
item.description: Authors show that after 2 or 3 primary doses and a first yearly booster dose, a second yearly booster dose of VLA15, an investigational Lyme disease vaccine, induced robust immune responses among participants 5 − 65 years of age and did not raise safety concerns.

item.title: Nature Communications: Vibrio cholerae -synthesized tryptophan activates innate immune signaling in enteroendocrine cells via phosphorylation of the nuclear receptor ultraspiracle
item.description: Although Vibrio cholerae forms a biofilm in the arthropod intestine, specificity in this interaction has not been demonstrated. Here the authors show that V. cholerae initiates a signaling cascade in host enteroendocrine cells that increases expression of Peritrophin 15a, a host factor that promotes V. cholerae colonization.

item.title: Nature Communications: Multi-omics integration unravels four molecular subgroups of corticotroph pituitary neuroendocrine tumours with distinct clinicopathological features
item.description: Corticotroph pituitary neuroendocrine tumours (PitNETs)/adenomas are heterogeneous sellar neoplasms that lack molecular-based classification. By performing multi-omics analysis of 270 corticotroph PitNETs, the authors identify four distinct molecular subgroups.

item.title: Nature Communications: Large language models decode narrative pathology reports to define clinically relevant subtypes in IgA nephropathy
item.description: Kidney pathology reports contain rich information that structured assessment does not fully capture. Here, the authors show that large language models extract and standardize it to define reproducible IgA nephropathy subtypes that improve risk prediction and reveal differential treatment responses.

item.title: Nature Communications: Non-enzymatic hepatic ABHD6 interacts with Akt-FoxO1 axis to regulate metabolic health
item.description: Selective hepatic insulin resistance contributes to the development of metabolic disease, but the molecular mechanisms \remain unclear. Here, the authors identify a nonenzymatic role for ABHD6 in promoting selective hepatic insulin resistance through modulation of Akt–FoxO1 signaling.

item.title: Nature Communications: Genome-wide DNA methylation analysis revealed epigenetic mechanism underlying end-stage renal disease
item.description: A two-stage epigenome-wide study identified 52 DNA methylation markers associated with end-stage renal disease across diverse primary kidney diseases, highlighting the shared roles of inflammation, immune dysregulation, and renal fibrosis.

item.title: Nature Communications: A foundation model for sleep-based risk stratification and clinical outcomes
item.description: Clinical sleep studies generate rich physiologic data, yet traditional metrics capture only part of their predictive value. Here, the authors show that a foundation model trained on thousands of recordings learns latent sleep patterns that cluster patients into clinically meaningful risk groups.

item.title: Nature Communications: Ruxolitinib prevents irreversible autoimmune endocrinopathies in APECED
item.description: APECED is a monogenic autoimmune disorder resulting from deleterious variants in the Autoimmune Regulator gene. Here, the authors report the cases of two patients with APECED in whom early intervention with the JAK1/2 inhibitor ruxolitinib prevented endocrine autoimmunity.

item.title: Nature Communications: Corisin induces proteostasis stress to drive epithelial injury and pulmonary fibrosis
item.description: Here, the authors establish the naturally occurring microbiota-derived Corisin as a potent driver of lung injury and fibrosis, revealing a previously unrecognized microbial pathway that disrupts epithelial cell function and promotes pulmonary fibrosis.

item.title: Nature Communications: High-throughput engineering of bispecific antibodies to enhance macrophage-mediated cytotoxicity of B-cell lymphoma
item.description: B-cell lymphomas can resist macrophage-mediated phagocytosis through different mechanisms. Here the authors present the results of a high-throughput system to screen for antibodies enhancing macrophage-mediated cytotoxicity of B-lymphoma cells, proposing a bispecific antibody comprising a SIRPα decoy domain and a CD38 targeting arm as therapeutic candidate.
